title: Checkup signal, or screen noise?
intro: Eight observations from a portfolio review — file each as one of the four real checks, or as noise.

cards.text: The SIP hasn't grown though income rose twice since it was set
Equity has crept from the planned 60% to 74% after the rally
Three of your five funds hold the same eight heavyweights
Unrealized gains have crossed the annual tax-free harvesting limit
The portfolio is down ₹18,400 since breakfast
A fund fell two places in this week's category rankings
Today's biggest loser in your folio is flashing red
A finfluencer says this month's NFO 'can't be missed'

debrief: The four checks share two properties: they run on a yearly clock, and each one ends in a decision you can actually take (raise the SIP, rebalance, consolidate overlap, harvest gains). The noise bucket shares the opposite: it updates fast, feels urgent, and leads to no decision a plan would endorse. The daily P&L is the purest specimen — 'anxiety with a green-and-red interface.' If an observation can't change what you'd do on a yearly clock, it isn't a check.
